questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The police arrested / two young men / but neither of them were / responsible for the robbery.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'but neither of them were'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'but neither of them was**' should be used instead of** 'but neither of them were'.**
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is as follows:
 
• Neither of+Plural Noun/Pronoun+Singular Verb.
 
 
• Example: *Neither of them looks after him.*
 
 
 
• Hence, '**was**' should be used.
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is** Option 2**.

 

**Correct Answer:__*** The police arrested two young men but **neither of them was **responsible for the robbery.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहाँ, **'but neither of them were' **के स्थान पर** 'but neither of them was' **का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• इस प्रकार के वाक्यों की संरचना इस प्रकार है:
 
• Neither of+Plural Noun/Pronoun+Singular Verb.
 
 
• Example: *Neither of them looks after him.*
 
 
 
• इसलिए, '**was**' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर** विकल्प 2** है।

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Earlier, they had to look through hundreds of mugshots in large books and they could make a positive identification only in 5% of the cases.

B. This saves a lot of time and effort and also leads to more positive identifications.

C. Now computers make this easier for witnesses by projecting only pictures that match the descriptions closely.

D. After a crime, witnesses often give the police a description and thus help to identify the criminal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'DACB'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Sentence D will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence explaining how the witnesses give a description of a crime to the police.
 
• Sentence A will be the next sentence because it further explains Sentence D.
 
• Sentence C will be the next sentence because it explains how computers help them.
 
• Lastly, Sentence B will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• D: After a crime, witnesses often give the police a description and thus help to identify the criminal.
 
• A: Earlier, they had to look through hundreds of mugshots in large books and they could make a positive identification only in 5% of the cases.
 
• C: Now computers make this easier for witnesses by projecting only pictures that match the descriptions closely.
 
• B: This saves a lot of time and effort and also leads to more positive identifications.

 
 
 

Correct Sequence:__ *After a crime, witnesses often give the police a description and thus help to identify the criminal. Earlier, they had to look through hundreds of mugshots in large books and they could make a positive identification only in 5% of the cases. Now computers make this easier for witnesses by projecting only pictures that match the descriptions closely. This saves a lot of time and effort and also leads to more positive identifications.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. The other was a ruffled, glum-faced man, heavily built and roughly dressed.

B. One man had a handsome presence with a bold and frank look.

C. But the most striking thing was that they were handcuffed together.

D. The two men who boarded the train from Denver were an odd pair.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'DBAC'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Sentence D will be the first sentence because it is an **introductory** sentence.
 
• Sentence B will be the next sentence because it further explains **Sentence D.**
 
• Sentence A will be the next sentence because it explains how they looked.
 
• Lastly, Sentence C will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• D: The two men who boarded the train from Denver were an odd pair. 
 
• B: One man had a handsome presence with a bold and frank look.
 
• A: The other was a ruffled, glum-faced man, heavily built and roughly dressed.
 
• C: The two men who boarded the train from Denver were an odd pair. 

 
 
 

Correct Sequence:__ *The two men who boarded the train from Denver were an odd pair. One man had a handsome presence with a bold and frank look. The other was a ruffled, glum-faced man, heavily built and roughly dressed. The two men who boarded the train from Denver were an odd pair. *
